moments.text: The winter is long and hard. Snow buries the lower villages, and the old die quietly in their beds, as the old always have.
Spring comes late this year. The plum trees bloom in the snow, and the village elders argue about what it means.
The Lantern Festival fills the valley below with light. From your terrace, it looks as if the stars have come down to drink.
The harvest moon hangs fat and orange over the fields, and the whole valley smells of new rice and rice wine.
A wandering singer has made a song about you. You hear it in every teahouse this year, and it gets your best fight wrong.
Letters come this year from far places: a coast you have never seen, a desert city, a temple in the clouds.
Fighters you have never met now claim to be students of your students, and some of them bow to you in the market without quite knowing who you are.
The rains come early and stay. The rivers rise brown and fast, and every roof in the province leaks.
A dry summer. The wells drop, the rice yellows, and the villages hold rain rites that the sky ignores.
Word comes that another friend of your youth has died. There are fewer of you every year who remember how it was.
The cicadas are loud this summer, louder than anyone can remember. The young complain. You find you like them.
The first snow falls in the night. In the morning the whole mountain is new and silent.
A new emperor takes the throne. Proclamations are posted in every town, and nobody in the mountains reads them.
The maples on your mountain turn red all at once this autumn, as if someone gave an order.
You notice the year has turned again only because the swallows are back under your eaves. The years go faster now.
The village at the foot of your mountain has become a town. There is a market now, and a magistrate, and a great deal of noise.
The dragon boat races come to the river town below. Drums carry up the valley from dawn till dark.
Locusts come out of the west this summer, a brown cloud that eats the sky. The farmers beat pots in the fields.
A fever runs through the towns of the province. Doors are marked, and the funeral bells ring every day.
Bandit gangs fight a war of their own in the southern hills this year. Smoke from burned granaries rises some evenings.
A new martial school opens in the county town, with a big gate and bigger promises. Its students strut in the market.
Tomb-sweeping day comes. All over the hills, families tidy the graves and burn paper money, and the smoke smells of spring.
It is a year of weddings. Red sedan chairs go up and down the valley, and the drums never seem to stop.
The river floods in high summer and moves its bed half a mile east. Whole fields are gone, and new ones appear.
The sun goes dark at noon for the space of a few breaths. Dogs howl, priests shout, and then the birds start singing again.
The magistrate raises the grain tax again. In the teahouses, people curse the capital in low voices.
Children in the town play at martial masters with stick swords. One of them always has to be the villain.
Cherry blossoms fall like rain on the temple hill this spring. Young couples climb it in the evenings.
A great fire burns half the market town in a single windy night. By midsummer, the new roofs are already going up.
The geese fly south early this year in long ragged lines. The old farmers say it will be a cruel winter.
War burns in the eastern provinces. Refugees come west with carts and children, and the price of rice doubles.
A new sword style is all the rage this year. Every young fighter in the Murim copies it, flourishes and all.
The great sects call a Murim conference this year. Banners and delegations pass through the valley for months.
The townsfolk have built a small shrine to you by the river. They leave oranges there and pray for good harvests.
The great tournament is held in the capital this year. Every inn is full of young fighters with more pride than sense.
Rumours spread of a demonic cult rising in the north. The sects close their gates early, and the night watches double.
Peace is signed on the northern border after thirty years of skirmishes. Old soldiers come home to farms they no longer recognise.
An old sect you once knew falls this year, its last elder dead and its halls sold. Its name will be forgotten within a generation.
Poets gather on the lake below for the autumn moon. Their verses drift up on the wind, some of them quite bad.
Silk caravans from the far west reach the province for the first time in a lifetime. The markets fill with strange spices and stranger stories.
The earth shakes in the spring. Old walls crack, a pagoda leans, and the hot springs run warmer for a month.
One of your old disciples has founded a sect of their own. Its students say your name in their morning oath.
A fog settles on the province in autumn and does not lift for a month. Sounds carry strangely, and everyone speaks softly.
The imperial examinations are held this year. Lamps burn all night in every scholar's window.
The great river threatens to break its dikes all summer. Whole counties turn out with baskets of earth.
A comet hangs over the world all autumn, its tail across half the sky. Every sect master reads it differently.
You have become a story told to children. Some of them do not believe you are still alive. Some believe you cannot die.
The old dynasty falls. A new one rises in its place, and its envoys ask politely where you stand.
The qi of heaven and earth swells this year, a tide felt by every cultivator in the world. Breakthroughs come easily, and so do madnesses.
Two of the great masters of your generation pass away this year. The Murim feels larger and emptier at once.
Five-coloured clouds gather over your mountain for nine days. Pilgrims arrive, certain it means something about you.
The year is a round number in the calendar, and the Murim marks it with long toasts to the oldest masters alive, whether you like it or not.
The young now name a whole school of fighting after you. You do not recognise half of what they teach under your name.
The orthodox sects and the demonic path circle each other all year like old dogs. Everyone waits for someone to bite.
Pilgrims climb to your gate every season now, asking blessings you are not sure you can give.
Stars fall in a great shower on the night of the autumn festival. In the morning, three villages each claim a fallen star.
Heaven is strangely quiet this year. No tribulation clouds over the great peaks, no omens in the stars. The silence itself feels like one.
The grave of an old rival of yours, dead these sixty years, has sunk into the hillside. The stone is older than you remember. So are you.
Mapmakers in the capital have drawn your mountain on the imperial map, with a small symbol that means dangerous. You are quietly pleased.
A calm settles over the valley below. The passes are quiet, the markets are busy, and nobody quite trusts it.
Spring comes to heaven, which here means the clouds turn faintly green and the jade trees chime when the wind passes.
The Queen Mother's Peach Banquet is held this century. Every immortal pretends not to care whether they are invited.
The Star River runs high this year, silver and roaring. Its spray falls to the world below as shooting stars.
You look down through the clouds and realise that a whole century has passed below while you were thinking.
A feud breaks out in the Jade Court between the Ministry of Thunder and the Ministry of Rain. Nobody below can predict the weather.
Tribulation clouds gather all year over a distant peak of heaven. Someone up here is about to be tested.
Heaven's winter comes once in a hundred years. Snow falls upward from the clouds and freezes into small stars.
The years up here blur together. Last year was much like this one, and you begin to understand why some immortals sleep for centuries.
A herd of qilin passes through the heavenly meadows, and for a season the grass grows gold in their hoofprints.
It is the Double Seventh. The Weaver Girl and the Cowherd meet on the magpie bridge, and all heaven pretends not to watch.
The prayers rising from below are louder this year. A war, a flood, a plague: the mortal world is having a bad century.
The Moon Palace opens its gates for the Mid-Autumn feast, and the scent of cassia drifts across all of heaven.
One of the sun's three-legged crows has escaped its post. The days below run long and hot while the court hunts for it.
The Jade Court counts its immortals this century. Clerks with very long scrolls visit every cloud, including yours.
The Dragon Kings come to court to receive their rain quotas for the coming century, and argue about every drop.
You catch yourself remembering the taste of mortal rice, plain and hot, and it is the strongest feeling you have had in years.
Lights of every colour ripple across heaven's sky for a whole season. The old immortals say the stars are restless.
A new mortal ascends this year, wide-eyed and still dusty from the world below. You remember being that.
The great bell of the Jade Court rings once at the turn of the century, and every cloud in heaven trembles.
One dawn the light comes up in colours there are no mortal words for, and you stand watching it until noon.
This century the junior immortals are made to sweep the Southern Heavenly Gate, and you are glad it is not you.
Your cloud lodging is small and drafty and faces the wrong way. The senior immortals' clouds block your view of the stars.
Rumours run through the lower courts of heaven: promotions, demotions, and a scandal involving a jade rabbit.
The heavenly gardens are given new keepers this century, and the lower immortals receive the worst plots by seniority.
The phoenixes molt this year. Their fallen feathers burn small holes in the clouds, and the junior immortals patch them.
You are homesick for the world below, though everyone you knew there is long gone.
The lower heavens hold their own small festival, with plain cloud cakes and borrowed music. It is better than the grand ones.
A heavenly clerk has misspelled your name in the Register of Immortals, and nobody seems to know how to fix it.
You are assigned to watch a minor star this century. It does very little. You grow fond of it.
The Hall of Celestial Learning opens its lectures to new immortals this century, and the benches are hard.
You have a seat at the Jade Court now, near the back. From there you can see every feud in the hall.
Rumours spread of unrest in the demon realms beyond heaven's edge. The celestial generals polish armour they have not worn in ages.
A new star is born in the east of heaven, and the court debates for a year what to name it.
It is the Jade Emperor's birthday, a ten-thousand-year one. Heaven holds a feast that lasts a mortal decade.
An immortal you know is cast down to the mortal world this year, for a crime nobody will name.
The great wheel of the cosmos turns one notch. Only the oldest immortals feel it. This year, you do.
A sky whale swims slowly above heaven itself, its shadow covering the Jade Court for a whole month.
The heavenly springs run low this century. Immortals queue politely at the Jasper Pool and glare at each other impolitely.
Envoys from the demon realms come to the Jade Court under a flag of truce, and all heaven watches them like hawks.
For a whole season heaven forgets to make evening. Immortals go about squinting and short-tempered.
Winter comes early and stays. Snow lies deep in the high valleys, and the weaker things of the forest do not see spring.
The thaw comes all at once. Every stream on the mountain roars, and the air smells green again.
Autumn comes. Below the forest, the humans cut their rice and sing, and the smell of new grain drifts up the slopes.
The geese pass over in long lines, calling. They have done this every year you can remember, and you remember many.
The summer rains come hard. The rivers burst their banks, and the animals of the lowlands climb toward higher ground.
The village below has grown again. Where there were six roofs when you were young, there are sixty now.
It is the hunters' season. Horns sound in the valleys at dawn, and every creature in the forest is wary.
The humans have left offerings at the old shrine on the hill again: rice, roasted chestnuts, a bowl of clear wine.
A dry year. The springs shrink to trickles, and the deer come to drink at dusk, nervous and thin.
You realise the little pine by the stream, a seedling when you were young, now stands as high as your shoulder. You remember it small.
The moon is very bright this year. The nights are silver, and the qi of the moon falls like fine dust.
Lightning sets the far ridge burning in late summer. For weeks the sky is brown and the air tastes of ash.
Drums and pipes rise from the villages for days: a human festival. The smell of roasting chestnuts reaches the trees.
The cicadas come up out of the earth this summer after many years asleep, and the forest roars with them.
The first snow falls in the night. In the morning the forest is silent and new, and every track tells a story.
The foxes on the hill have raised a new litter this spring. The cubs tumble about in the sun, fearless and foolish.
Humans have built a new farmhouse at the edge of the forest. Its dog barks at everything, including the wind.
A good year for berries. Every bush on the slope hangs heavy, and the bears are fat and lazy.
Village children come to the edge of the forest this summer, daring each other to go further in.
Storms roll in one after another this season, and every hollow and gully runs with water.
An owl has taken the old pine as its own this year. Every night it calls, and every small thing goes quiet.
The fish run upriver this autumn in their thousands, and every hungry thing for miles comes to the water.
Woodcutters work the lower slopes this year. Their axes ring through the trees from dawn to dusk.
Fog fills the valleys every morning this spring, and the world is only as big as the next tree.
A wolf pack has moved into the next valley. You hear them sing at night, and you listen.
The humans have built a small shrine to you at the forest edge. They are not sure what you look like, so the carving guesses.
A hermit monk has built a hut on your mountain. The smell of incense and plain rice drifts on the wind.
There is war among the humans. Smoke rises over the far plains, and armies with banners pass through the valley.
The humans are building a great wall of stone across the pass below, hauling rock all year.
The sun goes dark at midday. Every bird stops singing, and the humans below bang pots to frighten something away.
Ghost lights dance over the marsh every night this autumn. Something old is awake out there.
The villagers have a story about you now. Parents use it to keep children out of the forest after dark.
The mountain shivers in the spring. Rocks slide, a spring moves, and the qi of the earth shifts underfoot.
A sickness moves through the deer this year. The forest is quieter, and the crows are fat.
Humans have begun to climb the mountain in small groups, with incense and bells, looking for the spirit of the forest.
A comet hangs over the mountains all autumn. The humans below are frightened. The old spirits of the land are restless.
The humans have a new king, and then another. From your height, their kingdoms rise and fall like tides.
The humans have built a great temple on the next peak, with your likeness painted on its gate in gold.
Heaven's thunder rolls over the mountains all year, though the sky stays clear. You feel it calling.
Another long span of years turns. The forest has burned and grown back since you were young. You remember both.
The qi of heaven and earth rises like a tide this year. Every spirit on the mountain feels it, and grows bold.
A royal hunt comes to the mountains: hundreds of riders, banners, hawks and horns. They are looking for something great.
Strange lights ripple across the northern sky for a season. The spirits of the land say the stars are shifting.
The great lake freezes solid for the first time in a hundred years. The humans walk out onto it, amazed.
The old spirits of the land gather this year, as they do once a century, in the mist on the highest peak.

happenings.text: A letter comes from a disciple you taught decades ago. It is long, warm and full of questions about a technique.

effects.log: Three nights of writing. Explaining it, you understand it better yourself.
"Practise more." Somehow, it is exactly what they needed.
The letter sits on your desk all year, accusing you gently.

happenings.text: A young fighter climbs your mountain to challenge you, sword already drawn and hands shaking.

ok.log: You lose a sleeve and win the bout. The youngster leaves glowing.

fail.log: Holding back is harder than fighting. You take a cut you did not need.

effects.log: The sword goes back in its sheath by the second cup.
The youngster waits three days, then leaves. The town calls it cowardice.

happenings.text: A painter asks to paint your portrait for the provincial hall, and brings far too many brushes.

effects.log: Nine days of sitting still. The portrait makes you look wiser than you feel.
The painter paints you from memory anyway. The nose is wrong.

ok.log: Your brushwork is rough but alive. The painter weeps a little.

fail.log: Your painting looks like a radish in a robe.

happenings.text: Your herb garden needs you this year: the soil is tired, and the ginseng in the shaded bed is sulking.

effects.log: Months on your knees in the dirt. The roots come back strong, and so do you.
The boy is careless but cheerful, and the garden survives.
Weeds win. A few wild herbs move in that you never planted.

happenings.text: An old wound from a fight you barely remember begins to ache every morning.

effects.log: The acupuncturist is young and very nervous. It works anyway.
A season of slow work. The ache fades into a memory.
It aches all year, a small reminder that you were once careless.

happenings.text: A grand-disciple you have never met arrives at your gate, bowing so low the hat falls off.

effects.log: You teach for months. The young one is slow, but stubborn in the right way.

ok.log: Good roots. You send word that the line is in safe hands.

fail.log: You push too hard. The youngster limps home, and a stiff letter follows.

choices.text: Feed them and send them home

effects.log: Rice, soup, a pat on the head. Some visits only need that.

happenings.text: A scholar asks to write down your life, and arrives with a cart of blank paper.

effects.log: Your mistakes go in with the rest. The book is better for it.
Each fight grows with the telling. The scholar writes very fast.
Some lives are not for reading.

happenings.text: Two villages below quarrel over a stream, and both send their headmen up to you to settle it.

ok.log: You split the water by season. Both villages grumble, which means it is fair.

fail.log: Your ruling pleases nobody, and both send you worse rice this year.

effects.log: A month of digging with your own hands. Both villages bring you their best wine.

choices.text: Tell them to settle it themselves

effects.log: They do, eventually, with fists.

happenings.text: Clearing an old chest, you find the notebook you kept when you were young, full of clumsy diagrams.

effects.log: The young fool who wrote this guessed at things you forgot long ago.

choices.text: Give it to a struggling student

effects.log: Your clumsy diagrams make more sense to a beginner than any master's.
The young fool goes up in smoke. You feel lighter.

happenings.text: You sleep badly all year. The dreams are full of people you outlived.

effects.log: The dreams grow quieter, then kinder.
A long round of graves with wine and incense. You sleep afterwards.
It does not stop. It only gets blurrier.

happenings.text: A thief breaks into your hall one night and is very surprised to find you still awake.

ok.log: One hand on a collar. The thief confesses everything, including things you did not ask.

fail.log: Your knees are not what they were. The thief is gone over the wall.

effects.log: A hungry farmer, not a thief. You send the farmer home with rice.
The thief takes a candlestick and leaves an apology.

happenings.text: A rich merchant offers to pay for a new hall on your mountain, if the hall can carry the merchant's name.

effects.log: The hall is handsome and the name is large.
The merchant sulks, then pays anyway, for the story.
The mountain stays as it was.

happenings.text: Your old cook retires after forty years, and the new one is young, eager and burns everything.

effects.log: By winter the rice is good. So is your patience.
Your knife work is excellent. Your seasoning is a disgrace.
Charcoal is said to be good for the stomach. It is not.

happenings.text: A pair of red-crowned cranes nests on the roof of your hall. People come from three villages to see them.

effects.log: They raise two chicks. The town calls it a blessing on you.
A season watching cranes. Your footwork grows lighter.
A copper a look. The cranes are unimpressed.

happenings.text: A cough settles in your chest at the turn of the season and refuses to leave.

effects.log: A whole season in bed. You hate it. It works.
Bitter, black and effective. You are still the best herbalist on this mountain.
The cough wins every argument.

happenings.text: Village children creep up to your gate every evening, daring each other to ask you for a story.

effects.log: They listen with their mouths open. One of them will remember it in a hundred years.
They run screaming, and come back every night for more.
They decide you are a ghost. It becomes a local legend.

happenings.text: Sitting in the sun one afternoon, you see something in your oldest technique that you have missed for most of your life.

effects.log: Weeks of practice. The old move turns into something new.
A thin booklet. It will outlive you.
Some insights are for one afternoon only. It was a good afternoon.

happenings.text: A family below asks you to speak at the funeral of the old rice seller who fed your hall for seventy years.

effects.log: You speak plainly about rice and kindness. Half the village weeps.
The family is honoured, and a little disappointed.
You light incense alone that evening. Nobody sees it.

happenings.text: You find rust on the sword you carried in your youth. You do not remember the last time you drew it.

effects.log: The blade comes up bright. So does something in you.

choices.text: Give it to a worthy student

effects.log: The student trembles accepting it. That is the right way to receive a sword.
It watches the room like an old friend.

happenings.text: Farmers from the valley come to ask your help: a gang has been taking their grain for months.

ok.log: The gang leaves the county in one night. The farmers send you their first sacks.

fail.log: There are more of them than the farmers said. You win, at a cost.

choices.text: Teach the farmers to defend themselves

effects.log: Months of drills with hoes and staffs. They are terrible, then good.
The farmers go down the mountain in silence.

happenings.text: The county magistrate invites you to a banquet, mostly to be seen beside you.

effects.log: Eleven courses and twelve speeches. You are seen.

choices.text: Attend, and say what you think

effects.log: Your toast about the grain tax is remembered for years.
The magistrate is offended for a month and polite for a decade.

happenings.text: A rich family offers a cart of silver if you will take their spoiled heir as a student, gently.

choices.text: Take the heir, and the silver

effects.log: A year of complaining. By winter the heir can hold a horse stance for an hour.

choices.text: Take the heir, refuse the silver

effects.log: Nobody has ever refused their silver. The heir starts paying attention.
The family tells everyone you are past it.

happenings.text: The well in your courtyard silts up and gives only mud.

ok.log: Sweet water at forty feet. Sore arms, cold tea.

fail.log: Rock. Only rock. You haul water from the stream for weeks.

effects.log: You cross the courtyard with your eyes closed and point. They dig. Water.
They charge too much and sing too loudly.

happenings.text: A wandering monk stops at your gate for a night and stays a month, arguing about emptiness over tea.

ok.log: You win nothing and learn a great deal.

fail.log: The monk takes your best argument apart with one sentence.

effects.log: Listening to the monk, you hear what you think.
Emptiness, it turns out, includes sweeping. The courtyard has never been cleaner.

happenings.text: The town below asks you to judge the martial display at its festival.

effects.log: The best child wins, not the magistrate's nephew. The town loves you for it.
Nobody cries. Nobody learns anything either.

ok.log: A single form, slowly. The crowd goes quiet, then roars.

fail.log: You slip on a wet stone in front of everyone.

happenings.text: A farmer swears a fox spirit is stealing chickens, and begs you to deal with it.

ok.log: An ordinary fox. You move it far away, and the farmer tells everyone you banished a demon.

fail.log: A whole night in a henhouse. The fox comes the next night, when you have gone.

effects.log: You draw a squiggle on paper. The chickens stop vanishing, for reasons of their own.
Sound advice, badly received.

happenings.text: The old bridge the market town depends on gives way under a loaded cart, and the town has no money to rebuild it.

effects.log: It is named after you, to your great embarrassment.
A month of hauling timber four oxen could not move. Children follow you every day.
They build a ferry instead. It sinks twice.

happenings.text: A stranger arrives with a promissory note your younger self signed sixty years ago, with interest.

effects.log: The interest is extraordinary. So is your honour.

ok.log: You settle on the original sum and a good dinner.

fail.log: The lender's grandchild is a far better haggler than you.

effects.log: It is not. You both know it.

happenings.text: The local scholars hold a poetry contest and dare you to enter, sure that a fighter can only rhyme sword with sword.

ok.log: Your verse about an old blade wins second place. The winner bribed someone.

fail.log: It rhymes sword with sword. The scholars are delighted.

effects.log: You give the prize to a shy student at the back, the best by far.
A fighter who knows when not to fight is rare. They note it.

happenings.text: A grateful family sends you a horse: old, swaybacked and convinced it is a warhorse.

effects.log: It follows you around the courtyard like a large proud dog.
It pulls a plough happily for ten more years.

choices.text: Ride it once, for its pride

effects.log: Twice round the courtyard, then it stops to eat a bush.

happenings.text: Two young people from feuding families beg you to marry them in your hall before their parents find out.

effects.log: Their parents arrive furious and leave, months later, as in-laws.
A shouting match in your courtyard. Nobody is married, and everybody is angry.

choices.text: Bring both families to one table

ok.log: Two feuds end over one dinner.

fail.log: Two feuds become three.

happenings.text: A child from the village goes missing on your mountain, and the whole village comes up with torches.

ok.log: You find the child asleep in a hollow tree, perfectly happy.

fail.log: The dogs find the child first. You find a very surprised badger.

effects.log: Lines across the slope, a call every ten paces. The child is found by dawn.

happenings.text: You decide, at your age, to learn to brew rice wine properly.

effects.log: The first jar is vinegar. The third is excellent.
It ferments in a day and tastes of lightning.
The wine seller is relieved. You were bad for business.

happenings.text: The great bell of the valley temple cracks with a note heard across the valley, and the abbot asks if you can help.

ok.log: The crack seals. The bell rings truer than before.

fail.log: The crack spreads with a terrible note.

effects.log: The new bell carries your name on the inside, where only the bell knows.

choices.text: Tell them to ring it anyway

effects.log: A cracked bell. The monks decide it sounds humble.

happenings.text: The grandchild of an old enemy comes to your gate, not for revenge, but to ask what the grandparent was like.

effects.log: Neither of you likes the story. Both of you are glad to have heard it.
The grandchild leaves comforted. It was not a lie, quite.
Some doors stay closed.

happenings.text: An old tiger has come down from the high forest to take livestock, and the hunters of three villages beg your help.

ok.log: One shout of qi sends it back into the deep forest. It does not return.

fail.log: The tiger is old and clever. You come back scratched and empty-handed.

choices.text: Track it and lead it far away

effects.log: A long chase. The tiger lives, far from people, and so do the people.
They lose two dogs and a lot of nerve, but they win.

happenings.text: Envoys from a great sect arrive with gifts and a request: they want you as an honoured elder, in name only.

effects.log: Your name on their gate brings them students and you a stipend.
You inspect their halls and fix ten wrong stances in an afternoon.
The envoys bow and take back the gifts, slowly, in case you change your mind.

happenings.text: Refugees from the fighting reach your mountain: forty people with nothing but children and cooking pots.

effects.log: A long season of crowding and noise. Forty people live who might not have.

choices.text: Send them to the temple with silver

effects.log: The abbot takes them in. Your silver buys a great deal of millet.
They move on. You hear them for a long time.

happenings.text: Word comes that someone in the next province is using your name, teaching your techniques badly for silver.

ok.log: A hungry young fighter, terrified to meet you. You teach the techniques properly.

fail.log: The impostor is long gone, with the silver of four towns.

effects.log: Now everyone can learn your techniques badly for free.
Being impersonated is a kind of fame.

happenings.text: A master of your own generation writes, inviting you to one last duel on the mountain where you first met.

ok.log: The duel lasts all afternoon and ends in laughter. Neither of you will see such a day again.

fail.log: Your old friend wins, and is gentle about it.

effects.log: Wine and memories on the mountain instead.
The reply comes: "Coward. Stay well." You keep the letter.

happenings.text: One of your disciples is caught selling your hall's secret manual to a rival school.

effects.log: The hall is quieter, and a little afraid of you again.

choices.text: Forgive, and set a hard penance

effects.log: A year of hauling water. The disciple's loyalty afterwards is fierce.

ok.log: The rival school sells it back, embarrassed.

fail.log: They have already copied it twice.

happenings.text: A provincial warlord sends a sealed letter: come and train the warlord's army, and name your price.

effects.log: The warlord does not write again, which is its own kind of message.
You teach soldiers to stand and breathe, and leave before the war starts.

ok.log: The warlord laughs, then listens. One fewer war this year.

fail.log: The warlord laughs and does not listen.

happenings.text: A jealous official bans a copy of your teachings and burns it in the provincial square.

effects.log: The second version is half as long and twice as clear.
Banned books travel fastest.
Paper burns. Teaching does not.

happenings.text: A plague town sends for anyone who knows the meridians. The doctors there are dying faster than the sick.

ok.log: You save hundreds. Some call you a living immortal. You are only tired.

fail.log: You save some, and the fever nearly takes you too.

effects.log: Carts of herbs leave your mountain for months.
Nobody on your mountain falls sick.

happenings.text: A rival school mocks your style in a pamphlet, with insulting drawings.

ok.log: Their master apologises after one exchange. The pamphlets vanish.

fail.log: Their master is better than the pamphlet. You both bow and agree to say nothing.

effects.log: They are quite funny. You hang one in your hall.

choices.text: Answer with a pamphlet of your own

effects.log: Your drawings are worse. The feud becomes a beloved provincial joke.

happenings.text: The last heir of a fallen sect brings you its only surviving manual and asks you to keep it alive.

effects.log: A dead style breathes again in your courtyard.
A year of letters, silver and patience. A small hall reopens.
Some things are not yours to open.

happenings.text: Recruiters come through the valley taking the young for the army. Mothers climb your mountain to beg.

ok.log: The officer decides this valley has given enough.

fail.log: The officer writes your words into a report you will never see.

choices.text: Hide the young on your mountain

effects.log: Twenty youngsters learn to chop wood and keep quiet for months.
The empire takes what it takes.

happenings.text: A famous calligrapher begs you to write two characters for the gate of a new academy.

ok.log: Two characters full of qi. People come to see them for a hundred years.

fail.log: The brush feels like a sword in the wrong hand.

choices.text: Let the calligrapher write, and sign it

effects.log: Shared credit. Both of you look better.
The gate stays blank, and that becomes its own story.

happenings.text: A lamp tips over in the night, and your library hall catches fire.

ok.log: Armfuls of books through the smoke. The hall is lost; the knowledge is not.

fail.log: The smoke drives you back. Half the books are ash.

effects.log: Everyone lives. The books do not. You know which you chose.
One breath, a great wind. The fire dies, and so do three windows.

happenings.text: A tea master from the south arrives with leaves picked from a single ancient tree, and offers you a cup.

effects.log: One cup, a whole spring in it. Your qi settles like still water.

choices.text: Trade a technique for the tree

effects.log: A fair trade. Neither of you will ever tell.
The tea master drinks both cups without complaint.

happenings.text: The townsfolk swear a ghost haunts your mountain on moonless nights, in old-fashioned robes like yours.

ok.log: Your own reflection in a polished temple gong, seen by a drunk. You laugh for a week.

fail.log: You see something, once, and decide never to speak of it.

effects.log: Fewer thieves. More pilgrims.
You chant the words, loud and solemn. The town feels better.

happenings.text: A master in a far province proposes a game of go played by letter, one move a month.

effects.log: Twelve moves this year. Each one a small essay of intent.

ok.log: Your opponent resigns in a beautiful letter.

fail.log: Your opponent was waiting for exactly that.

effects.log: At your age, months count differently.

happenings.text: An imperial messenger arrives with a gift from the throne: a jade plaque, a bolt of silk, and expectations.

effects.log: The plaque hangs in your hall. Officials bow to it, and so to you.
Your thank-you letter is so polite it promises nothing at all.
Brave. The throne remembers.

happenings.text: Two kingdoms at war both send envoys to ask which side you favour. Your answer could end the war.

ok.log: Both kings sign in your hall. The war ends within a year.

fail.log: Both kings leave insulted. The war goes on.

effects.log: Neither king is happy. Neither attacks your mountain.
The war is theirs. You have trees to tend.

happenings.text: The great sects, split into camps again, ask you to preside over their council for a decade. Every other candidate is younger and hungrier.

effects.log: A year of meetings. You settle three feuds and start one.
A good choice, and everyone knows whose choice it was.
They argue for a year without you.

happenings.text: Your most gifted grand-disciple hovers on the edge of a breakthrough, and the qi in the hall is restless.

ok.log: It holds. A new master is born under your roof.

fail.log: The qi turns wild. You draw it into yourself, and pay for it.

choices.text: Let the youngster face it alone

effects.log: The breakthrough comes on its own, rough but real.

choices.text: Give up a pill of your own

effects.log: Your last good pill, gone. The breakthrough is smooth.

happenings.text: A demonic master you defeated long ago is rumoured to be alive, and recruiting.

ok.log: An upstart using the old name. You end the upstart's career.

fail.log: It is no rumour. You fight to a draw, and both withdraw.

effects.log: The Murim takes your warning seriously. That alone scares the recruits away.

choices.text: Wait for it to come to you

effects.log: Nothing comes this year. You stay ready.

happenings.text: The province raises a stone statue of you in the capital square. It is twice your size and half your age.

effects.log: The crowd cheers the statue more than you.
You stand before your own stone face for a long time.
The capital gets a well with your name on it. It is used every day.

happenings.text: Lightning strikes your mountaintop three times on a cloudless day. Your qi answers each strike.

choices.text: Climb up and sit in it

ok.log: The fourth strike never comes. What remains in the air feeds you for a month.

fail.log: The fourth strike comes.

effects.log: You feel each echo in your meridians.
Prudence is also a technique.

happenings.text: The last other master of your generation sends word: there is something to say before the end.

effects.log: Three days of talk. At the end you understand each other perfectly, for the first time.
Your letters cross. Both say the same thing.
The silence says it too, less kindly.

happenings.text: The great tournament asks you to give the opening demonstration, before ten thousand spectators.

ok.log: Ten thousand people hold their breath at once.

fail.log: A perfect technique, slightly mistimed. Only the masters notice. They notice a lot.

effects.log: The young laugh. The masters do not.
You watch from the crowd, unrecognised, eating a skewer.

happenings.text: A ragged orphan with frighteningly good bones has been sleeping in your woodshed for months.

choices.text: Take the orphan as a disciple

effects.log: The last disciple of your long life. Possibly the best.

choices.text: Find the orphan a good sect

effects.log: A letter from you opens any gate.
Some help should not have a name.

happenings.text: A qi storm rolls across the province, and your mountain sits in its eye.

ok.log: You drink the storm. Your meridians sing for weeks.

fail.log: Too much, too fast. A month of repairing yourself.

effects.log: Your qi wall holds all night. The village sleeps safe.
It passes. Your mountain is greener afterwards.

happenings.text: The Emperor asks you to teach the crown prince for a year. The crown prince is twelve and terrible.

effects.log: By the end of the term the prince can sit still. A year on, think. History will thank you quietly.

ok.log: The prince grows into a good ruler, and is a little afraid of you forever.

fail.log: The prince complains to the Emperor. You are thanked and sent home.

effects.log: The Emperor finds a less wise tutor.

happenings.text: A landslide opens an ancient cultivator's tomb on your mountain. Every sect wants in.

effects.log: Some dead deserve their sleep.

ok.log: Old notes on a forgotten breathing method.

fail.log: Traps, still working after a thousand years.

effects.log: A year of chaos and treasure hunters. Somebody finds something.

happenings.text: Your old sword begins to hum at night, as if it remembers every fight it ever had.

effects.log: It leads you through forgotten forms till dawn.

choices.text: Wrap it and let it rest

effects.log: It sleeps. So do you, better than in years.

ok.log: It teaches you something about your younger self.

fail.log: It hums louder and louder until you drop it down the well.

happenings.text: Famine grips three provinces. Your name could open the granaries of the great sects, if you use it.

effects.log: The sect granaries open. Some sects never forgive you for it.
Your hall eats thin gruel for months. Nobody complains.
The famine runs its course. The silence is loud.

happenings.text: Your disciples and an old rival's disciples have started a feud in both your names, over nothing at all.

choices.text: Meet the rival and end it

effects.log: Two old masters drink together in public. The feud dies of embarrassment.

choices.text: Let them settle it in a match

ok.log: Your side wins narrowly, and graciously.

fail.log: Your side loses, and sulks for a decade.

effects.log: Your disciples sweep the courtyard for a year. The feud ends from one side.

happenings.text: One morning you wake with the clear sense that you have learned everything this world can teach you.

effects.log: There is always something. This year it is how to rest.
Teaching it, you find it was not everything.
Heaven is still there, waiting.

happenings.text: A sect from the far southern islands sends a master to compare techniques with you, invited by nobody.

ok.log: A beautiful exchange. Both styles change a little.

fail.log: The island style is strange and fast. You lose, and are delighted.

effects.log: Six weeks of tea and diagrams. Your style gains a new curve.
The master leaves a carved shell at your gate.

happenings.text: You are seated at a celestial banquet between two immortals who have not spoken to each other in three thousand years.

ok.log: By the third course they are laughing. Heaven owes you a small favour.

fail.log: By the third course they are throwing peach stones, and you are in the way.

effects.log: The food is extraordinary. So is the silence.
The junior is thrilled. You eat in the kitchens, where the cooks are better company.

happenings.text: A small heavenly beast, part lion and part cloud, wanders onto your terrace and refuses to leave.

effects.log: It eats starlight from your hand and purrs like distant thunder.

choices.text: Return it to the Beast Garden

effects.log: The keeper bows to you. The beast sulks for a century.

ok.log: It learns to sit. All heaven is amazed.

fail.log: It learns to sit on you.

happenings.text: A poetry gathering is held on a floating pavilion, and you are expected to compose a verse about eternity.

ok.log: It is carved on a jade tablet and argued over for a century.

fail.log: Eternity, it turns out, is hard to rhyme.

effects.log: The oldest immortals weep. They had forgotten rice.
Some of the verses took a thousand years to write.

happenings.text: A mortal prayer reaches you directly, by some accident of heaven's clerks: a village asks for rain.

effects.log: A gentle rain falls on one valley below. The Ministry of Rain files a complaint.

choices.text: Forward it to the right ministry

effects.log: It will be answered in a century or two.

ok.log: Rain falls, soft and quiet. Nobody up here notices.

fail.log: Hail falls instead. You hope nobody below saw your face.

happenings.text: Two factions of the Jade Court each ask, very politely, which of them you support.

effects.log: Thunder remembers its friends, loudly.
Rain remembers its friends, quietly.
Both factions call you wise behind your back and difficult to your face.

happenings.text: A fellow immortal invites you to fish in the Star River, where the catch is small stars and the bait is old memories.

choices.text: Bait with a memory of home

effects.log: You catch a small blue star. It warms your qi for a decade.

choices.text: Bait with a memory of a fight

effects.log: You catch something hot and angry, and put it back.
The river is so beautiful that fishing seems rude.

happenings.text: A celestial general challenges you to a friendly bout. In heaven, friendly bouts last a month.

ok.log: You win on the twenty-ninth day. The general laughs so hard the clouds shake.

fail.log: You lose on the thirtieth day, honourably.

effects.log: You both call it a draw. You both know who was ahead.
The general finds someone else to bruise.

happenings.text: You are asked to tend a heavenly peach tree that fruits only when it chooses. This year it has chosen.

effects.log: One peach, perfectly ripe. The Queen Mother sends thanks.
Only a fallen one, so it barely counts. Your qi glows for days.

ok.log: Two peaches this cycle. The gardeners are astonished.

fail.log: The tree sulks and fruits a century late.

happenings.text: A mortal in the world below dreams of you every night and has built you a shrine. You feel each stick of incense.

effects.log: You appear and say something kind. The mortal tells the whole province.
The mortal's rice grows a little better. That is all, and enough.
The smell of incense follows you for a decade.

happenings.text: You decide to grow a garden on your cloud. The soil here is mostly light.

ok.log: They bloom at night and sing faintly.

fail.log: They bloom at noon and shriek.

effects.log: It grows, shiny and odd. It tastes of home.
Light is a garden already.

happenings.text: The Hall of Heaven's Law holds a great debate: should immortals interfere in the mortal world?

effects.log: You lose the vote, but not the argument.
You win the vote. Something about it sits badly with you.

ok.log: Both sides claim you. The law is amended slightly, and wisely.

fail.log: Both sides disown you.

happenings.text: Heaven's qi falls as rain for a single day, and every immortal is out on the clouds with a cup.

effects.log: Your meridians fill like rice fields in spring.
The junior immortals cultivate on your gift for years.
Undignified. Wonderful.

happenings.text: An ancient immortal, bored beyond telling, asks you to say something they do not already know.

ok.log: They had not looked down in eight thousand years. They are fascinated.

fail.log: They knew it all already, and are disappointed.

effects.log: They laugh for the first time in four thousand years. Heaven shakes.
That, they say, is the first true thing anyone has said in a century.

happenings.text: You are given a star-lantern to carry in the procession of a celestial festival. It is heavier than it looks.

ok.log: Your steps are perfect. The lantern lights half of heaven.

fail.log: You stumble once, and a small star falls to the world below.

effects.log: You carry a small lantern near the back, happily.

happenings.text: The Jade Rabbit of the Moon has been grinding elixir and has, it says, made a little too much.

effects.log: It tastes of moonlight, with a hint of carrot.
A season at the pestle. Your arms are strong and your nose glitters.
The rabbit is not pleased with you.

happenings.text: Another immortal faces a tribulation and asks you to stand witness, close enough to be scorched.

ok.log: Your presence steadies them. They survive, and owe you forever.

fail.log: A bolt catches you. You both survive, crisply.

effects.log: You bear honest witness from afar.
Your qi joins theirs. You are hollow for a season, and they live.

happenings.text: The Celestial Archives open one stack to visitors this century. The stack is the size of a mountain.

effects.log: Ten thousand mortal dynasties. Patterns appear.
Only the index. Even that changes how you think.
A short entry. Accurate, and a little unkind.

happenings.text: A new immortal settles on the cloud beside yours and plays the zither badly every morning, for a decade.

effects.log: A decade later the playing is good. A century later, beautiful.
The paperwork for moving a cloud takes eleven years.
Eventually you do. It becomes the sound of home.

happenings.text: A star slips from its place and begins to fall. You are the closest immortal.

ok.log: You catch it and put it back. The Star Ministry commends you.

fail.log: It burns through your sleeves and falls to the world below.

effects.log: They catch it at the last moment, with much shouting.
Somewhere below, a child sees a shooting star and makes a wish.

happenings.text: An old immortal invites you to a tea ceremony that takes forty years to complete.

effects.log: Forty years, one cup. It is perfect.
The first decade alone teaches you patience.
You have places to be, though in heaven that is never quite true.

happenings.text: A celestial painter wants you in a mural of the Immortals of the Age, near the edge.

effects.log: Ten years of standing still. You are in the mural, slightly blurred.

choices.text: Ask to be in the middle

effects.log: You are moved to the middle, and then quietly back.
The painter paints a cloud where you would have been.

happenings.text: You find a pool that shows whatever you most want to remember.

effects.log: Your first master's face, exactly. You sit by the pool for a year.
Some memories are better a little blurred.

ok.log: It shows a small kindness you will one day do. It comforts you.

fail.log: It shows only fog.

happenings.text: At a feast the immortals play a riddle game, and the losers must sing.

ok.log: Nine of ten. Three senior immortals have to sing.

fail.log: You must sing. Heaven is very quiet afterwards.

effects.log: A mortal song from your village. The immortals are strangely moved.

happenings.text: The guard of the Southern Heavenly Gate has dozed off, and asks you to stand in for a day.

effects.log: Nothing comes through. One cloud tries.

ok.log: A hundred stories in a single day.

fail.log: A very senior immortal does not enjoy being questioned.

effects.log: The guard is grateful, and terrified.

happenings.text: You notice an immortal at court whose shadow moves a moment after the body does.

ok.log: A demon in disguise. The court is in your debt.

fail.log: An ordinary immortal with an ordinary shadow problem. Embarrassing for everyone.

effects.log: The Ministry investigates quietly. You never learn the answer.
The shadow catches up eventually. Probably nothing.

happenings.text: You are tired in a way only an immortal can be. A century of sleep tempts you.

effects.log: You wake rested, and heaven has hardly noticed.
You stay awake and watch. Watching is its own rest.
Your dreams are full of stars.

happenings.text: A senior immortal hands you a broom and points at a cloud covered in peach stones.

effects.log: The cloud shines. Seniors notice who sweeps.

choices.text: Sweep with a wind of qi

effects.log: One breath. The stones fall to the world below as a rain of peach trees.
You are given a worse one: polishing thunder.

happenings.text: You are summoned before a minor deity for the first time, and nobody tells you the protocol.

ok.log: The deity is charmed by your mortal manners.

fail.log: You bow to the wrong statue for an hour.

choices.text: Copy whoever is next to you

effects.log: They are new too. You both bow to the wrong statue.

happenings.text: A senior immortal keeps taking credit for your work in the Ministry ledgers.

ok.log: One look at your qi, and the ledger is corrected.

fail.log: They are senior for a reason.

effects.log: Credit in heaven is a long game.
In a century, the truth comes out.

happenings.text: Your cloud keeps drifting sideways. The other junior immortals call it the Crab.

ok.log: It flies straight. Mostly.

fail.log: Now it drifts in circles.

effects.log: A sideways cloud is, in its way, distinctive.

happenings.text: The junior immortals sit an exam on celestial law. It is ninety thousand lines long.

ok.log: You pass in the top tenth. A small post is offered.

fail.log: You fail on line forty thousand.

effects.log: You pass the parts about mortals and nothing else.

happenings.text: You find a hole in the clouds through which you can see your old home far below.

effects.log: Strangers live there now. They seem happy.
A good harvest falls on your old valley.
You mend the cloud. It is easier.

happenings.text: You are sent with a message to the Ministry of Thunder. Nobody has told you where it is.

ok.log: You arrive early, which in heaven is suspicious but admired.

fail.log: You follow the wrong rumbling for a decade.

effects.log: The crane knows. Cranes always know.

happenings.text: Another junior immortal, who ascended in the same century as you, suggests you look out for each other.

effects.log: A friend in heaven is worth ten thousand pills.
Solitude has its own cultivation.

happenings.text: You are set to watch an elixir furnace that must not cool for nine years.

ok.log: Nine years awake. The elixir is perfect, and you are given a drop.

fail.log: You blink, once, in the seventh year.

choices.text: Feed it a little of your qi

effects.log: It stays warm, and so do you.

happenings.text: A small tribulation cloud forms over your cloud alone. It is the size of an ox, and very angry.

ok.log: Small lightning, small gain.

fail.log: Small lightning, real burns.

effects.log: It follows you for a while, then gets bored.

happenings.text: A brand-new immortal arrives, lost and frightened, and attaches to you like a burr.

effects.log: You remember how it felt. They never forget your kindness.
Efficient, and cold.

happenings.text: You are offered a small post: Keeper of the Seventh Lesser Gate. It is mostly about the hinges.

effects.log: The hinges have never been so well kept.
A century of training instead.

happenings.text: The Jade Court votes on sending a flood to punish a wicked mortal kingdom. Your vote is needed.

effects.log: The vote fails by one. The kingdom never knows.
Justice from heaven is heavy. You feel its weight.

ok.log: A small drought instead. The kingdom reforms, frightened.

fail.log: The court mocks your half-measure.

happenings.text: The celestial army needs a commander for a patrol at the edge of heaven.

ok.log: Three demon raids turned back. Your banner hangs in the Hall of Valour.

fail.log: A raid gets through. You stop it, at great cost.

effects.log: Your plans are good. Others get the glory.
Someone younger goes.

happenings.text: A rival from your mortal life, long ago, has ascended too, and comes looking for you.

effects.log: The old grudge looks small from up here.

ok.log: You win. It matters less than you thought.

fail.log: You lose. That matters less too.

effects.log: Heaven is large enough for two grudges.

happenings.text: A junior immortal begs to become your disciple. In heaven, an apprenticeship lasts ten thousand years.

effects.log: Ten thousand years of teaching begin with a single lesson.
The junior is promising.
The junior finds another master, and tells everyone.

happenings.text: The court asks you to name a newborn star.

choices.text: Name it for your first master

effects.log: A small bright star, forever, for someone long dead.
Vain, but now heaven cannot forget you.

choices.text: Name it for a mortal village

effects.log: In that valley, mortals look up at their own star for a thousand years.

happenings.text: You are chosen to speak with the demon envoys, because you remember mortal bargaining better than most.

ok.log: A thousand-year truce, sealed with your qi.

fail.log: The talks collapse. The envoys leave with threats.

effects.log: You learn more than the court will ever ask about.

happenings.text: You are asked to judge the case of an immortal accused of helping mortals too much.

effects.log: The court grumbles. The mortals below never know whom to thank.
The law is the law. You feel older.

choices.text: Sentence a century of service below

effects.log: A wise sentence. Both sides are unhappy.

happenings.text: Your own tribulation clouds gather, high and dark, though the time is not quite yet.

ok.log: The lightning finds you ready. Your body hardens.

fail.log: Too early. The lightning finds you wanting.

effects.log: A decade of stillness. They drift away, for now.

happenings.text: The Jade Emperor, by way of six ministers, asks you to carry a gift to the Dragon King of the Eastern Sea.

effects.log: The Dragon King is pleased, and sends back pearls and a long speech.

choices.text: Deliver it and stay for the feast

ok.log: The feast under the sea lasts a decade. You make a powerful friend.

fail.log: You offend the Dragon King's third cousin.

happenings.text: A senior deity asks you, idly, whether the mortal world is getting better or worse.

effects.log: The deity smiles. That was the hopeful answer.
The deity frowns. That was the honest answer.
The deity laughs and writes it down.

happenings.text: A phoenix offers to carry you to the edge of heaven, where the world ends in light.

effects.log: You stand at the edge of everything. Nothing is quite the same afterwards.
The phoenix goes alone, and brings you back a feather.

happenings.text: One of the oldest immortals is ascending beyond heaven itself, and asks you to see them off.

effects.log: They vanish into a light without colour. You feel the next step, faintly.
"Ask me again," they say, and are gone.

happenings.text: A hunter's snare lies hidden in the grass where you like to pass. You smell iron and human sweat on it.

effects.log: Snap. The hunter will find an empty snare and wonder.
You leave it for something less clever.
The hunter loses a good snare, and the forest is a little safer.

happenings.text: A small human child has wandered into the forest and sits crying under a tree as the light fails.

effects.log: You lead the child to the forest edge by sounds and shadows. The village tells the story for years.
You keep the dark away all night. The searchers find the child asleep and safe.
The searchers find the child at midnight. You were never there.

happenings.text: Another beast has come into your country this year, younger and hungry, marking your trees as its own.

ok.log: One fight, short and loud. It leaves and does not return.

fail.log: It fights harder than you expected. You both limp away.

effects.log: There is enough here for two, if both are careful.

ok.log: You let your old qi rise, once. It flees before it understands why.

fail.log: It is too young to know fear. It only grows curious.

happenings.text: You feel your age this year: slower to rise in the mornings, and slower to heal.

effects.log: Long days of warm stone and sleep.
You know the bitter ones that help.
Stubbornness keeps you moving.

happenings.text: A villager climbs to your favourite rock, leaves a bowl of rice and a handful of roasted chestnuts, and bows three times.

effects.log: Plain and good. The villager finds the bowl empty and runs home amazed.
The birds are delighted.
The villager falls flat in a bow and never forgets.

happenings.text: A small mountain spirit, like a child made of moss, comes to sit near you and stare.

effects.log: It stays the whole year, humming. The plants around you grow well.
It scolds you in a language of rustling leaves and vanishes.

ok.log: It tells you where the mountain qi pools in spring.

fail.log: It only hums. Still, a pleasant hum.

happenings.text: A storm drives a family of humans into the shelter of the rocks where you rest. They have not seen you.

choices.text: Stay still and let them shelter

effects.log: They sleep near you all night, never knowing.
You give them the rocks and take the rain.
They flee into the storm. You feel sorry, afterwards.

happenings.text: An old wound from a hunter's arrow, years ago, aches in the damp air.

effects.log: The warm water draws the ache out.
Slowly, the old knot loosens.
It aches. You endure.

happenings.text: A wild fruit tree on the slope has fruited so heavily that its branches crack.

effects.log: Sweet, ripe and heavy. A good day.
The small creatures of the slope eat well for a month.
The villagers who come to pick it go home empty and frightened.

happenings.text: A great eagle has started circling over your favourite resting place, a little closer every day.

ok.log: It veers off and finds another sky.

fail.log: It swoops. You both decide it was a mistake.

effects.log: Wisdom is not always about winning.

happenings.text: You sleep through a long grey season and dream of the place you were born.

effects.log: You wake knowing something old about yourself.
The dream fades, but its warmth stays.

happenings.text: On the brightest night of the year, the moon's qi pours down onto the high rocks.

ok.log: Your core drinks it like water.

fail.log: It slides off you like rain off stone.

effects.log: You do not cultivate. You only enjoy it.

happenings.text: A young woodcutter sings while working, every day, the same song, badly.

effects.log: By autumn you know the song. You could not say why it matters.
The singing stops. You miss it.
The woodcutter finds them and sings louder.

happenings.text: A hollow tree on the slope holds an old wild hive, heavy with honey, and the smell of it is everywhere.

ok.log: Stings, and a sweetness worth every one.

fail.log: The bees win this year.

effects.log: The hive thrives, and the slope is thick with bees for years.

happenings.text: An old monk sits on a rock near you every evening and talks to the forest as if it can hear.

effects.log: The monk talks of patience and rice and the moon. Some of it stays with you.
The monk smiles, as if expecting it all along.
The monk talks on to the trees.

happenings.text: A sudden surge in the river has stranded a family of deer on a shrinking island in the river.

ok.log: The deer cross on the logs, trembling, and are gone.

fail.log: The current takes the logs. The deer swim for it themselves.

effects.log: The river decides. It always does.

happenings.text: You spend a long clear night watching the stars wheel, and notice that one has moved since you were young.

effects.log: It moves a hair each year. Even stars go somewhere.
Stars can move without your help.

happenings.text: A new hot spring has opened in a cleft of rock. Steam drifts up from it.

effects.log: The heat goes deep, to the old aches.
Other creatures keep away. You soak alone, and feel a little lonely.
Monkeys, foxes and an old badger share the steam with you, uneasily at first.

happenings.text: A human comes to the forest edge every evening to weep over a grave that you can smell is fresh.

effects.log: Nothing troubles the mourner in your forest.

choices.text: Leave a flower on the grave

effects.log: The mourner finds it, and weeps a little less.
Grief is a human thing.

happenings.text: A fox has started stealing from your hidden stores of food. It is shameless about it.

ok.log: One pounce. The fox learns manners.

fail.log: It is quicker than you, and laughs at you in its way.

effects.log: One morning it leaves a dead mouse for you, as rent.

happenings.text: A village dog has started barking at the forest edge every night, at you.

effects.log: It barks all year, then grows old.

ok.log: It whines and hides under a house. The villagers wonder what it saw.

fail.log: It barks louder. The whole village comes out with torches.

effects.log: It wags at the forest after that. The villagers find this stranger still.

happenings.text: A ring of pale mushrooms has sprung up in a damp glade, and the air inside it hums faintly.

ok.log: Qi, sudden and warm.

fail.log: Strange dreams for a week, and a sore stomach.

effects.log: The humming settles into you.
Old instinct says no.

happenings.text: A bear in a foul temper roams your part of the forest.

effects.log: A wise season of hiding.

ok.log: The bear decides you are not worth it.

fail.log: The bear decides you are worth it. You flee, battered.

happenings.text: Village children have set a clumsy trap of sticks and a basket, baited with a sweet rice cake.

choices.text: Take the cake without springing it

effects.log: A perfect theft. The children argue about it for a month.
The basket falls on nothing. The children shriek and flee.
A crow takes the cake, and the blame.

happenings.text: A strange sweet scent drifts from a hidden cleft in the rocks, heady enough to make you dizzy.

effects.log: Flowers bloom there in a pocket of warm rock, out of season and out of reason. You roll in them. Undignified. Glorious.
The sweetness carries a little qi.

happenings.text: A hawk chick has fallen from somewhere high and sits squeaking in the grass.

effects.log: The parents come for it at dusk.

choices.text: Guard it till the parents come

effects.log: The hawks circle you, unsure, then take their chick.
Hidden from the foxes. The parents find it at dusk.

happenings.text: A sudden surge of water floods the low ground where you usually sleep, and you need a dry place fast.

ok.log: A dry cave, warm and empty.

fail.log: Every dry place is taken. You sleep wet.

choices.text: Share a hollow with a badger

effects.log: An uneasy night. The badger snores.

happenings.text: The farm at the forest edge keeps fat chickens behind a very poor fence.

effects.log: Easy. The farmer finds feathers and curses the forest.
The fence is a temptation you choose to ignore.

choices.text: Chase off the fox eyeing them

ok.log: The fox goes. The farmer never knows who guarded the chickens.

fail.log: The fox is faster.

happenings.text: The old boar that ruled the next ridge has died, and its country lies open.

effects.log: More ground, more food, more trouble.
Let the young fight over it.

happenings.text: Tiny lights rise from a hidden hollow in their thousands, as if the stars have come down to hunt.

effects.log: A long, still, beautiful night.

ok.log: A small spark of qi stays with you.

fail.log: Only pretty lights.

happenings.text: A big snake has claimed your favourite sunning rock and will not move.

ok.log: It slides off, sulking.

fail.log: It strikes. You win the rock and lose some dignity.

effects.log: It is a big rock. The snake ignores you for the rest of the season.

happenings.text: The old keeper of the shrine at the forest edge has stopped coming. The shrine goes unswept.

effects.log: You find the keeper sick in a hut below, and leave healing roots at the door every week until the keeper recovers.
You leave wild fruit in the bowl. The village is amazed.
Shrines, like humans, do not last.

happenings.text: A band of hunters with dogs and spears has come for you, not for deer. You are worth money now.

ok.log: They chase your scent into a bog and go home muddy.

fail.log: The dogs are not fooled. You escape, but only just.

ok.log: Spears break, dogs flee, hunters run. Nobody dies.

fail.log: A spear finds you before they run.

effects.log: You lose a season of feeding. They lose interest.

happenings.text: A wandering monk recites sutras on a rock every dawn. The words carry qi, faint and strange.

ok.log: The words begin to make a kind of sense.

fail.log: Words are human things.

effects.log: Your qi grows calm.
The dawns are quiet again.

happenings.text: The villagers below pray at your shrine for the weather to turn. Their fields are suffering.

choices.text: Turn the weather with your qi

ok.log: The weather turns kind for the village fields.

fail.log: Nothing changes but a breeze.

choices.text: Lead them to a hidden spring

effects.log: You let one villager see you near the water. A channel is dug before the year is out.
The weather turns late. The village blames you a little.

happenings.text: A human sorcerer is painting charms on the trees of your forest, trying to bind whatever lives here.

ok.log: The charms crumble. The sorcerer feels it and flees.

fail.log: The charms bite back.

effects.log: The sorcerer runs, leaving brushes and ink behind.
The charms bind nothing but squirrels.

happenings.text: Soldiers have camped in your valley on their way to war. They cut trees and shout at night.

effects.log: They leave in a month. The valley heals in a year.

ok.log: A terrible sound in the night. By morning the camp is empty.

fail.log: They hunt you for a week.

effects.log: A sack at a time. They blame each other.

happenings.text: A village healer comes into the forest for herbs and gets lost in the mist.

choices.text: Lead the healer to the herbs

effects.log: The healer fills a basket, finds the way home, and wonders all year.
The healer finds the way out, eventually.

happenings.text: The new carving at your shrine looks nothing like you. The villagers seem very proud of it.

effects.log: It is a kind of love, badly carved.
The carver faints, then carves a much better likeness.
They put it back up and add more offerings, worried.

happenings.text: A tiger of the deep mountains has heard of you and comes to see which of you is stronger.

ok.log: A long fight under the moon. The tiger bows its head and leaves.

fail.log: The tiger is stronger, this time.

effects.log: The tiger sits with you a while, then leaves. Respect, of a kind.

happenings.text: You find a spring whose water tastes of qi, hidden behind a fall of rocks.

effects.log: The qi is cool and strong.
Every year you return to it alone.
They build a little shrine beside the spring.

happenings.text: A scholar sits on a rock below and paints the mountain for weeks. You wander into the painting by accident.

effects.log: You are in the painting now, a shape in the mist, forever.
The painter will remember only a shadow.

happenings.text: Bandits have made their camp in a cave on your mountain, and rob the villagers in the valley.

ok.log: They leave at night, screaming about a mountain spirit.

fail.log: They have fire and spears. You pull back, hurt.

effects.log: You leave tracks a child could follow. The villagers do the rest.
Human trouble is for humans.

happenings.text: The king's huntsmen are searching the mountains for the great beast of the legends. They mean you.

ok.log: After a month they declare you a myth and go home.

fail.log: They corner you on a cliff. You escape through the clouds, hurt.

choices.text: Show yourself once, at a distance

effects.log: They hunt no more after that. They write poems.

ok.log: Not one hunter is hurt. Every weapon is.

fail.log: Archers. Many archers.

happenings.text: A messenger of heaven, a crane in silver light, lands near you and waits, as if expecting an answer.

effects.log: The crane bows back and departs. Heaven has noted you.
It waits three days, then leaves.

ok.log: In a voice like bells, it says that heaven is watching.

fail.log: It only stares.

happenings.text: A young human cultivator climbs your mountain every year, asking to learn from you.

effects.log: Without words, you show how qi moves. The young human weeps with gratitude.
You chase the youngster down the mountain. Next year, they come back faster.
They leave a bowl of rice and go.

happenings.text: Storms far upriver send a great flood toward the villages below. The river is rising past anything you remember.

choices.text: Turn the river with your qi

ok.log: The water bends away from the villages.

fail.log: The flood is bigger than you. You save one village of three.

choices.text: Carry the villagers to high ground

effects.log: All night you carry the old and the small up the slope.
The river takes what it takes.

happenings.text: An ancient serpent spirit from the next range claims your peak as its own.

ok.log: Three days of storm. It goes home.

fail.log: It is older than you. You yield the high peak for a decade.

ok.log: You trick it into claiming a peak that is all ice.

fail.log: It sees through you.

effects.log: Two great spirits, one sky. An uneasy century.

happenings.text: The monks of the great temple climb up to you with drums and banners, to honour you on your feast day.

effects.log: You let them see you. The drumming stops, and the chanting starts.
Your qi settles over their halls. Their crops grow well that year.
They chant anyway, to the clouds.

happenings.text: Heaven's thunder rolls right over your peak, and it seems to say your name.

ok.log: A bolt strikes you and leaves you stronger.

fail.log: A bolt strikes you and leaves you scorched.

effects.log: It is not time yet. You understand that now.

happenings.text: Human generals leave offerings at your temple, begging your help in their war.

effects.log: War is a human madness.

choices.text: Send fog to stop the battle

effects.log: Neither army can find the other for a week. They go home.
A shadow over their camp. They retreat, and your side takes their land.

happenings.text: You find the place where you came into the world. It is a village now, with a well where you were born.

effects.log: The villagers draw water and never know.
The water stays sweet for a thousand years.

happenings.text: Another great beast of the old legends sends word through the spirits: it wishes to meet.

effects.log: Two ancients on one peak, talking of the world as it was.

ok.log: It means only friendship.

fail.log: It tests your strength, roughly.

effects.log: Old beasts keep old distances.

happenings.text: A scholar has climbed your mountain to write your true history. You can smell the ink from a mile away.

effects.log: The history is accurate, and terrifying.
The history is full of mercy.
The history is mostly guesses.

happenings.text: A storm of raw qi breaks over the mountains, and the whole range glows.

ok.log: Your core swells with it.

fail.log: It tears through you.

effects.log: You calm the storm around your valley.

happenings.text: The clay settles a hair this year, as an old house settles. Above, a door that always stuck now shuts.

effects.log: Everything above you sits a little more truly. Someone says the house has a good feeling.
You keep the old height and the door goes on sticking. Some things are a kind of company.
You wake with the settling done. Nothing has fallen.

happenings.text: Children play a counting game on the ground over you, jumping from stone to stone. As far as you can tell, you are one of the stones.

effects.log: Nobody falls all year. The children think the game is lucky.
One child wobbles, laughs, and decides the game is better.
You reach thirty-one before the supper call. The number feels like a small gift.

happenings.text: Dew never settles on one patch of ground. The people have noticed, and have begun to leave a bowl of something there.

choices.text: Let it be a good sign

effects.log: The bowl fills with rice cake and the patch stays bare. Everyone is a little happier.
The dew comes back and the bowl goes away. You miss both.
Before long there is a green circle in the dust. They name a festival for it.

happenings.text: A well-digger is working nearby. In a month the shaft will pass within an arm of you.

effects.log: The well-digger tastes it and weeps with relief, and cannot say why.
The digger finds a hard layer and goes round. The well is good, a little crooked.
The shaft passes through your edge. For a moment you are a well, and cold, and useful.

happenings.text: A dog has taken to sleeping on the ground above you. It will not say why and will not be moved.

effects.log: The dog stretches out with a sigh. In a week it has told every dog in the district.
The dog sleeps. You keep a perfect stillness, as one does with a friend.
The dog lifts its head, tilts it, and stays exactly where it is.

happenings.text: You spend the year feeling each of the things that press on you: a wall, a well, a gatepost, a grave. Each is lighter than you feared.

effects.log: Nine weights. You can tell a mother's from a magistrate's.
The grave. It is only a very old patience. You carry it differently.
You are an earth that holds a house. It is what you are for, you decide.
